title: Understanding Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The bias-variance decomposition is a way to express the error of a model in terms of bias, variance, and irreducible error (noise). It helps in understanding how different factors contribute to the overall error.

title: Conditions for Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The decomposition holds under certain conditions, such as when the model is linear and the loss function is squared error. Consider whether these conditions apply to non-linear models.

title: Non-linear Models and Squared Loss
text: Non-linear models can still use the bias-variance decomposition if the loss function is squared error. The decomposition is not limited to linear models.

title: Applying Bias-Variance Decomposition to Non-linear Models
text: Given that the bias-variance decomposition can apply to non-linear models with squared loss, does this decomposition hold true for non-linear models and squared loss?
